# Write a story test

A story is one visitor's journey with one outcome, and its test reads like it. It lives in
`src/test/java/com/xoveconsulting/tests/cases/` with every other test (the generated ones, rebuilt from each crawl, and the
other stories); what they stand on (BaseTest, StoryTest, Story) is one folder up:

1. **One class per story, named after its id**: letters and digits kept, the first upper case
   (`engi-101` is `Engi101`, in `Engi101.java`). It extends `StoryTest` and carries
   `@Story(value = "<id>", title = "<title>")`; both are imported from `com.xoveconsulting.tests`.
2. **One `@Test`**, its `@DisplayName` the story's title.
3. **One chain**, from the page the story starts on, through what the visitor does (`navigateTo()`,
   `click()`, `enter()`, `check()`, `execute()`; a click that changes page returns the next page), to
   **one `verify()`** at the end: the story's outcome. Arriving on a page needs no check of its own:
   every page checks it has loaded (`get()`) when a step lands on it. Arriving on *which* page of a family
   (this product, not any product page) is an outcome: `verify().isThePageOf(...)`, with the arguments `open()` takes.
4. A method the chain needs and the page does not have: add it (add-an-action.md), don't reach
   around it with Playwright calls in the test.
5. Run `mvn test -Dtest=<StoryClass>,SuiteRulesTest`. SuiteRulesTest fails, naming the rule
   (SUITE-RULES.md) and saying what to write, when a story class lacks `extends StoryTest` or
   `@Story`, isn't named after its id, has more than one test or more than one `verify()`, does
   anything after its `verify()`, asserts, or uses a locator, Playwright or `Thread.sleep` itself.
   Evidence of a failure is saved for you (fix-a-failing-test.md): nothing to add to the test for it.

```java
package com.xoveconsulting.tests.cases;

import com.xoveconsulting.tests.Story;
import com.xoveconsulting.tests.StoryTest;
import com.xoveconsulting.tests.pages.home.HomePage;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.DisplayName;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;

@Story(value = "PROJ-1", title = "A visitor can open Xove Consulting Services from the header")
class PROJ1 extends StoryTest {

    @Test
    @DisplayName("A visitor can open Xove Consulting Services from the header")
    void story() {
        new HomePage(page).open()
                .navigateTo().xoveConsultingServices()
                .verify().isLoaded();
    }
}
```

A story with data ("with an invalid email") takes its data as plain strings in the test. Data that
differs between copies of the site comes from `SiteConfig.value("name", "default")`; a password
from `SiteConfig.secret("password")`.

A story that checks two things is two stories: push back and suggest the split (stories/AI-INSTRUCTIONS.md). One outcome per story means a failure points at exactly one thing.

**A story gone stale** (the feature changed or went away): delete its class from `cases/` and its file
from stories/done/. Nothing else depends on it. SuiteRulesTest reminds you if one is left without the
other.
